top_level_objectives: Identify the structural components of a DNA nucleotide and the 3D double helix.
Understand complementary base pairing rules and the specific hydrogen bonding between A-T and G-C.
Determine the 5' to 3' directionality of antiparallel sugar-phosphate backbones.
Describe the roles of helicase, SSBPs, DNA polymerase, and DNA ligase in unwinding and replicating DNA.
Differentiate between continuous leading strand synthesis and discontinuous lagging strand synthesis (Okazaki fragments).
Explain why DNA replication is a semiconservative process.

scenes.brief_purpose: Introduce the 3D double helix structure of DNA and the anatomy of a single nucleotide.
key_visuals: A large, slow-rotating 3D DNA double helix.
Highlighted sugar-phosphate backbones spiraling around a common axis.
An isolated, exploded view of a single nucleotide showing the phosphate group, deoxyribose sugar, and nitrogenous base.
student_actions: Rotate the entire DNA double helix to observe its major and minor grooves.
Extract a single nucleotide from the helix.
Identify and tap the phosphate, sugar, and base components on the extracted nucleotide to label them.

scenes.brief_purpose: Examine the specific hydrogen bonding rules between complementary nitrogenous bases.
key_visuals: A zoomed-in cross-section of the helix focusing on the base pairs in the center.
Visible, glowing dotted lines representing hydrogen bonds between bases.
Distinct molecular shapes for Adenine (A), Thymine (T), Guanine (G), and Cytosine (C).
student_actions: Count and select the correct number of hydrogen bonds for an A-T pair (2) and a G-C pair (3).
Drag and drop free-floating complementary bases to correctly pair them with a single exposed DNA strand.

scenes.brief_purpose: Understand the 5' to 3' and 3' to 5' antiparallel orientation of the two DNA strands.
key_visuals: A detailed, atomic-level view of the deoxyribose sugar rings on opposing strands.
Numbered carbon atoms (1' through 5') on the sugar rings.
Glowing directional arrows that superimpose over the backbones to show overall polarity.
student_actions: Trace the sequence of carbons on a sugar ring to identify the 5' phosphate end and the 3' hydroxyl end.
Tap both strands to reveal their opposite directional arrows, confirming the antiparallel layout.

scenes.brief_purpose: Demonstrate the initiation of replication at the replication fork using helicase and single-strand binding proteins.
key_visuals: A linear section of double-stranded DNA.
A 3D model of the helicase enzyme shaped like a rotary ring.
Small, stabilizing Single-Strand Binding Proteins (SSBPs).
student_actions: Drag the helicase enzyme onto the DNA origin site to begin separating the two strands, creating a replication fork.
Deploy SSBPs onto the newly exposed single strands to prevent the hydrogen bonds from reforming.

scenes.brief_purpose: Illustrate the continuous 5' to 3' synthesis of the leading strand by DNA polymerase.
key_visuals: The open replication fork with the 3' to 5' parental template strand highlighted.
A 3D model of the DNA polymerase enzyme.
A growing complementary strand rendered in a distinct bright color to differentiate it from the parental strand.
student_actions: Attach the DNA polymerase enzyme to the 3' end of the primer on the leading strand template.
Initiate synthesis and watch the polymerase glide smoothly toward the replication fork, adding nucleotides continuously.

scenes.brief_purpose: Explain the discontinuous synthesis of the lagging strand and the formation of Okazaki fragments due to the antiparallel constraint.
key_visuals: The 5' to 3' parental template strand (lagging strand).
Multiple DNA polymerase enzymes.
Short, disconnected segments of newly synthesized DNA (Okazaki fragments).
A 3D model of the DNA ligase enzyme.
student_actions: Place a DNA polymerase on the lagging strand and observe it synthesize DNA moving away from the replication fork, stopping when it hits a previous fragment.
Repeat this process to form multiple Okazaki fragments.
Apply the DNA ligase enzyme to the gaps to seal the sugar-phosphate backbone and connect the fragments.

scenes.brief_purpose: Visualize the final products of replication to confirm the semiconservative model of DNA replication.
key_visuals: Two complete, identical DNA double helices positioned side-by-side.
A color-coded rendering where parental strands are blue and newly synthesized strands are gold.
student_actions: Toggle a color-code filter to clearly distinguish the old parental strands from the new daughter strands.
Rotate both new helices to visually confirm that each final DNA molecule consists of exactly one original strand and one newly-synthesized strand.
